alternatives.assessment: A spatial map can reveal connections, but would compete with reading and create a heavier mobile experience.

alternatives.name: Literary Index
alternatives.assessment: A disciplined typographic index is useful, but alone would repeat the current edition's uniform rows.

typography.family: Self-hosted Manrope variable; existing Noto Sans Devanagari for Hindi
typography.display: Weight 650-750, tight but readable tracking, fluid 52-108px

homepage_sequence: Leave no question unasked: split typographic opening and tactile research object
Three real questions change the featured collection, synopsis and reading link
Curated selection across belief, economics, science and society
A short close reading as an approachable entry
Author portrait and statement on checking arguments
Research method and substantial contact footer
principles: Make actual research the subject of the design.
Use one memorable book interaction; keep navigation immediate and native scrolling.
Vary scale and composition instead of repeating rounded cards.
Keep readable content visible with reduced motion and without hover.
Use real metadata for counts, languages, links and sources.
implementation: React components and scoped CSS with native browser interactions
URL-backed archive filters; curated subject controls
Preserve shared reader manuscripts and download bytes
Full build, lint, preservation checks, browser interaction and responsive review
Local preview for the user's decision; no push or deployment

critical_review.risk: A large headline with generic cards could resemble a template.
critical_review.response: Use a typographic research object, true cross-disciplinary questions, an asymmetric selection and a compact reading desk. Avoid decorative video, scrolling capture and fake claims.
critical_review.boundary: The existing footer-only /white/ entry and Original/Observatory code remain untouched.
